# pmbook benchmark results (generated by tools/plot_latency.py)

## Internal latency: frame received -> book updated -> PMBook line published

| Run | frames measured* | p50 | p90 | p99 | p99.9 | max | service p50 | service p99 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Replay: naive (nlohmann + std::map + mutex) | 293,000 | 7.3 µs | 15.9 µs | 57.3 µs | 103.4 µs | 2915 µs | 4.67 µs | 20.48 µs |
| Replay: optimised (simdjson + flat + SPSC) | 293,000 | 1.8 µs | 3.7 µs | 13.6 µs | 28.2 µs | 605 µs | 1.47 µs | 4.09 µs |
| Replay: optimised, hybrid wait | 293,000 | 29.2 µs | 61.4 µs | 69.6 µs | 89.1 µs | 974 µs | 1.58 µs | 3.90 µs |
| Replay at 10x: optimised (colder caches) | 1,465 | 7.8 µs | 12.8 µs | 34.3 µs | 77.8 µs | 107 µs | 3.68 µs | 12.67 µs |
| Live: optimised, spin | 2,158 | 9.7 µs | 15.1 µs | 27.1 µs | 104.4 µs | 177 µs | 8.32 µs | 22.02 µs |
| Live: optimised, hybrid wait | 1,972 | 41.0 µs | 72.7 µs | 89.1 µs | 131.1 µs | 202 µs | 10.49 µs | 25.09 µs |

\* Frames that produced at least one published message (PONGs and frames for assets not yet snapshotted are excluded). Replay runs: the 12-minute shipped sample, 1,533 frames, replayed 200x at 1000x real-time gaps. Replay publishes into a sink that discards bytes; live runs write to a stdout pipe read by examples/consume.py.

## Throughput: processing only, one thread, no pacing

| Variant | frames | frames/s | µs per frame | books match live run |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| nlohmann::json + std::map book + std::mutex queue | 76,650 | 214,349 | 4.67 | True |
| simdjson + flat-array book + lock-free SPSC queue | 306,600 | 659,929 | 1.52 | True |

## Speed-ups (same data, same machine)

- internal latency p50: 4.1x lower
- internal latency p99: 4.2x lower
- internal latency p99.9: 3.7x lower
- service time p50: 3.2x lower
- throughput: 3.1x higher

Machine: Apple M5 | 10 cores | 16 GB | Darwin 25.6.0 arm64  
Build: clang 23.1.4  | Release | LTO on
